forced_by_bound.Aprime(0)=0: B|A'|/(2rA) bounded  =>  A(0) finite nonzero, A'(0)=0
forced_by_bound.conclusion: metric = eta_uv + O(r^2) in Cartesian coords: C^{1,1}, Lorentzian, centre is a manifold interior point

leg_i_not_sufficient.why: rho depends on r alone, so it is O(3)- hence O_h- hence -1-invariant, yet it is ODD in r. r^(2k+1) = (x^2+y^2+z^2)^((2k+1)/2) is a non-polynomial O_h invariant, which is the loophole a polynomial-only Reynolds argument leaves open.

leg_ii_not_necessary.why: every odd-degree T_d invariant carries xyz, whose monopole vanishes, so m(r) is unchanged and a non-centrosymmetric lattice gives the same regular centre in the f(r) channel

B2_point_group_nogo.verdict: the point-group route is CLOSED. The load-bearing hypothesis is smoothness/analyticity of the coarse-grained core density at the centre, not inversion symmetry.

B3_polynomial_parity.scope_limit: POLYNOMIALS ONLY. Non-polynomial O_h invariants such as r^3 = (x^2+y^2+z^2)^(3/2) are odd in r -- see B2(i).
B3_polynomial_parity.what_it_buys: given smoothness as a separate hypothesis, an anisotropic lattice density has no odd-degree Cartesian terms

B4_geodesics.E_eq_1_caveat: de-weighted: after tau = L ln(L/a) = 3.046 ticks the infaller is inside the central cell, where the model resolves no metric; the continuum law is extrapolation there
B4_geodesics.load_bearing: E>1 and null: they reach r=0 and must pass through, which requires B1's C^{1,1} interior point
B4_geodesics.nonradial: Lz^2/r^2 barrier diverges as r->0 since f(0)=1>0: no non-radial geodesic reaches the centre
B4_geodesics.null_radial: dr/dlam = +/- E: reaches and CROSSES the centre at finite affine parameter
B4_geodesics.scope: LOCAL r->0 analysis. NOT a completeness proof for the maximal extension, which for a two-horizon core requires the full conformal diagram.

B5_parity_screen.bonanno_reuter_note: BR carries an odd r^3 from the linear alpha*r in its denominator, so it sits in ZM's incomplete class. Reported as this screen's output; we have found no paper stating or disputing it and claim no priority.
B5_parity_screen.screen_scope: adjudicates the ANALYTICALLY-even class only; metrics that are smooth but flat at the origin (CSV and its even modification) are out of scope and are reported as such, not scored

B6_scales.ceiling_fork_is_open: F183 and F284 imply ceilings differing by a factor 24 in K (24^(1/4) in length); under F284's the core radius is L = a exactly and the e-folding is sqrt(3) ticks = one cell crossing = F284's own t_min. Open decision.
B6_scales.saturation_is_an_assumption: without saturation as an EQUALITY every scale is a one-sided bound: L >= 24^(1/4) a, etc.

B7_resolvability.M_crit_note: core one cell across; NOT a black-hole threshold
B7_resolvability.M_ext_note: horizon disappears below this: sub-~19-Planck-mass black holes do not exist in this model. This is the physically meaningful small-mass threshold.
B7_resolvability.covering_radius_note: simple-cubic inversion-centre array of spacing a/2; worst-case point (1/4,1/4,1/4) is Wyckoff 8c, site symmetry -43m = T_d

substrate_tier_not_counted.conclusion: chain length is unbounded: the substrate is tick-complete
substrate_tier_not_counted.criterion: Grant-Kunzinger-Saemann property (TC), with length = maximal causal chain length = tick count

premises.lattice_is_boundaryless: infinite, rigid, eternal (F283/F284); no boundary, no excised region
premises.update_is_norm_preserving: unitary, so no chain terminates for want of amplitude
premises.update_is_total: the BCC rule is defined at every cell for every neighbourhood configuration

substrate_tier_not_counted.sufficiency: NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- it does not forbid the emergent affine parameter saturating while ticks run on. B1 is what rules that out.

title: Lattice core geodesic completeness from bounded curvature; point-group route to the parity condition is a no-go
